title: Pope Leo Goes to Meet Attila
text:
In 452 Attila, king of the Huns, invaded northern Italy. He destroyed the city of Aquileia and took Milan and other cities of the Po valley. The Western Roman Empire seemed helpless, and Rome itself appeared to lie open before him.

The emperor Valentinian III sent an embassy to Attila. It was led by Pope Leo I, together with two senior Roman officials, the former consul Gennadius Avienus and the former prefect Trigetius. They met the king near the Mincio River, close to Mantua.

The chronicler Prosper of Aquitaine, a contemporary who knew Leo, wrote that Attila received the embassy and was so pleased by the presence of the high priest that he ordered his army to stop and withdrew beyond the Danube, promising peace. Attila died the next year.

Later legend added that the apostles Peter and Paul appeared behind Leo with drawn swords, threatening Attila, a scene Raphael painted in the Vatican. Historians point to more practical reasons as well: Attila's army was suffering from famine and disease, and the Eastern Roman emperor had sent troops against the Huns' homeland.
lesson: Going in person to face someone who threatens you can achieve what force cannot. Courage and dignity at the table are a form of power.
people: Pope Leo I, Attila, Gennadius Avienus, Trigetius
location: Near the Mincio River, Mantua, Italy
source: Prosper of Aquitaine, Epitoma Chronicon, year 452; Jordanes, Getica 42
caveat: Other factors, including disease and famine in the Hun army and Eastern Roman attacks, probably weighed as much as Leo's persuasion.
